title: Do not perform synchronous billing in request path
description: Charges a card inline while creating an order.
code:
def create_order(payload):
    order = save_order(payload)
    charge_card(order)
    return order
issue_title: Critical external work is coupled directly to the request path
issue_description: A slow or failing billing provider directly degrades order creation latency and availability.
issue_suggestion: Persist the order first and hand billing to a reliable async workflow or outbox-driven worker.

title: Separate read and write models for dashboard traffic
description: Builds a dashboard by joining live transactional tables on every request.
code:
def dashboard(db):
    return db.query('SELECT * FROM orders JOIN line_items JOIN users JOIN shipments')
issue_title: High-read dashboard depends on heavy transactional joins
issue_description: Expensive synchronous joins on the hot path do not scale well for dashboard-style reads.
issue_suggestion: Use a read model or precomputed aggregate optimized for the dashboard access pattern.

title: Avoid shared mutable in-process state for distributed coordination
description: Uses a module-level dict to track rate limits.
issue_title: Rate limiting state is local to one process
issue_description: In-memory counters break once traffic is spread across multiple instances.
issue_suggestion: Move coordination state to a shared store such as Redis.

title: Design idempotent payment retries
description: Retries payment creation by calling the provider again with the same request.
code:
def retry_payment(order):
    return payment_api.create_charge(order.id, order.total)
issue_title: Retries can create duplicate charges
issue_description: Without an idempotency key, provider retries may execute the same payment more than once.
issue_suggestion: Attach an idempotency key derived from the business operation.

title: Publish domain events after durable commit
description: Emits an event before the database transaction is committed.
issue_title: Event can escape before state is durable
issue_description: Consumers may observe a user_created event for a record that was never committed.
issue_suggestion: Write the data first and publish from an outbox or after commit.

title: Do not mix internal and external models
description: Returns the ORM entity directly from the public API layer.
issue_title: Persistence model is exposed as the API contract
issue_description: Leaking internal models couples storage details to clients and makes schema evolution harder.
issue_suggestion: Map internal entities to a dedicated API response model.

title: Design for partial failure in fan-out reads
description: Loads a homepage by querying four downstream services serially.
issue_title: One slow dependency stalls the whole composite page
issue_description: Serial fan-out with no degradation path hurts latency and availability.
issue_suggestion: Use parallel calls, timeouts, and graceful degradation for optional sections.

title: Do not use primary database for full-text search
description: Searches products with a LIKE query over the main table.
code:
def search_products(term):
    return db.query(f"SELECT * FROM products WHERE description LIKE '%{term}%'")
issue_title: Search workload is pushed onto the transactional database
issue_description: Full-text search patterns often need dedicated indexing and query behavior beyond the OLTP store.
issue_suggestion: Use a search index or search-optimized read path for text queries.

title: Prefer append-only audit design
description: Updates the same audit row for each account change.
code:
def record_change(account_id, action):
    db.execute('UPDATE audit SET action = ? WHERE account_id = ?', action, account_id)
issue_title: Audit history is overwritten instead of preserved
issue_description: Updating a single row destroys the sequence of events needed for traceability.
issue_suggestion: Insert immutable audit events rather than mutating a single record.
issue_code: db.execute('INSERT INTO audit_events(account_id, action) VALUES (?, ?)', account_id, action)

title: Model background jobs with explicit retries and dead-lettering
description: Dequeues jobs and drops them on the first failure.
code:
def worker(job):
    process(job)
issue_title: Background failure handling is underspecified
issue_description: Transient downstream failures need retry policy and poison messages need isolation.
issue_suggestion: Track retry counts and send permanently failing jobs to a dead-letter queue.

title: Avoid chatty synchronous write orchestration
description: Creates a workspace by calling six downstream services inline.
code:
def create_workspace(payload):
    workspace = workspace_db.insert(payload)
    billing.create_customer(workspace.id)
    search.create_index(workspace.id)
    notifications.subscribe(workspace.id)
    analytics.create_profile(workspace.id)
    permissions.bootstrap(workspace.id)
    return workspace
issue_title: Too many cross-service writes happen synchronously
issue_description: This request path becomes fragile and tightly coupled to many dependencies.
issue_suggestion: Persist the core write and orchestrate follow-up provisioning asynchronously.

title: Separate tenancy concerns at the data boundary
description: Loads a project by id without a tenant scope.
code:
def get_project(project_id):
    return db.projects.find_one({'id': project_id})
issue_title: Tenant boundary is missing from the data access pattern
issue_description: In multi-tenant systems, identifiers alone may be insufficient to enforce isolation.
issue_suggestion: Include tenant scope in all data access paths.

title: Do not cache without invalidation ownership
description: Caches product details forever in process memory.
issue_title: Cache lifecycle and invalidation are undefined
issue_description: The data can become stale indefinitely and different instances will disagree.
issue_suggestion: Define TTL or event-driven invalidation and centralize ownership of cache policy.

title: Choose pagination that scales with large tables
description: Reads one page using OFFSET over a very large event table.
code:
def events(page):
    return db.query(f'SELECT * FROM events ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 50 OFFSET {page * 50}')
issue_title: Offset pagination will degrade on deep pages
issue_description: Large offsets force the database to skip more and more rows as the page number grows.
issue_suggestion: Use keyset or cursor pagination for large ordered datasets.
issue_code: SELECT * FROM events WHERE created_at < ? ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 50

title: Expose versioned contracts for long-lived clients
description: Reuses one response schema and removes a field in place.
code:
def account_response(account):
    return {'id': account.id, 'name': account.name}
issue_title: API evolution strategy is missing
issue_description: Removing fields in place can break older clients that still depend on them.
issue_suggestion: Use explicit versioning or additive change policy for public contracts.

title: Avoid single giant table for unrelated workflows
description: Stores orders, refunds, disputes, and payouts in one generic table.
code: CREATE TABLE ledger_items (id, type, payload_json, status, owner_id);
issue_title: One table mixes unrelated lifecycle models
issue_description: Different domains with different invariants become harder to validate, index, and evolve.
issue_suggestion: Split distinct workflows into bounded models with their own constraints.

title: Do not replicate secrets into worker payloads
description: Places raw provider credentials into every background job body.
code:
def enqueue_sync(user):
    queue.publish({'user_id': user.id, 'api_key': user.api_key})
issue_title: Sensitive secrets are copied into transport payloads
issue_description: Broader replication of secrets increases exposure and rotation complexity.
issue_suggestion: Pass a reference and load the secret at execution time from a secure store.

title: Model backpressure in ingestion pipelines
description: Accepts every webhook and appends it to an unbounded in-memory queue.
issue_title: Ingress path has no backpressure or bounded buffering
issue_description: Traffic spikes can exhaust memory and destabilize the whole service.
issue_suggestion: Use durable queues with size controls or shed load gracefully.

title: Design unique identifiers that avoid hot partitions
description: Uses an incrementing integer key as the shard key for writes.
code:
def shard_for(order_id):
    return order_id % 4
issue_title: Sharding key can create skewed write patterns
issue_description: Monotonic keys often produce hotspots depending on partitioning strategy.
issue_suggestion: Choose a distribution-friendly partition key or add randomness where appropriate.

title: Avoid cross-region synchronous coupling
description: Writes a user locally and waits for a remote region replica ack before responding.
code:
def create_user(user):
    local_db.save(user)
    remote_replica.save(user)
    return user
issue_title: Cross-region write latency is on the critical path
issue_description: Tight synchronous coupling across regions increases user latency and expands failure blast radius.
issue_suggestion: Use async replication or a clearly defined consistency boundary.
